To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of a capillary LC system with a Nanomate device for the second dimension of a two-dimensional LC/MS system enables the identification of a higher number of metabolites compared to the combination of the Nanomatte with the capillary LC system.

the combination of the two-dimensional LC/MS approach and the chip-based nanoelelctrospray device with a qTOF mass spectrometer is a very useful tool for the structural elucidation of unknown metabolites.

a two-dimensional LC/MS system using either a capLC/MS or Nanomate as the second dimension is a powerful tool for metabolite identification in human ADME studies using a quadrupoles time-of-flight mass analyzer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies for the identification of metabolites in biological samples.
the development and application of a novel approach for the structural elucidation of unknown metabolites using a Nanomate and a qTOF mass spectrometer.
the development of a new method for the structural elucidation of drug metabolites using the Nanomate and the qTOF mass spectrometer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two methods complement each other and both are required for a complete structural characterization of metabolites.

the Nanomate system is a powerful tool for the structural elucidation of drug metabolites in the case of high abundant metabolites and that the capillary LC/ MS system is more suitable for the analysis of trace metabolites.
both techniques, the Nanomate and the capillary LC/NS system, have their advantages and disadvantages and are complementary to each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two-dimensional LC/MS system is a very powerful tool for the structural elucidation of drug metabolites.

the Nanomate is a powerful tool for structural elucidation, especially in cases of stable, high abundant metabolites, whereas the capillary LC/ESI-MS system is more appropriate to analyze trace metabolites.
a combination of the two methods (Nanomated capillary LC/ MS) is the best approach to identify unknown metabolites from a complex matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Nanomate is a very useful tool for the structural elucidation of unknown metabolites in complex samples.
a two-dimensional LC/MS approach with a Nanomate as the second dimension is very suitable for the characterization of unknown metabolites in a biological sample.
the combination of a chip-based nanospray system with a qTOF mass spectrometer is an excellent approach to investigate unknown metabolites in biological samples.
